The proposed mechanism is version-controlled AI experiment proposals are checked against approved constraints, explicit epistemic uncertainty, randomized human-review queues and independent protocol authority. A competing account holds that reviewer anchoring, selective display, search-data leakage or choice-set truncation can create superficial human agreement. It is an engineering arrangement of bounded decisions, independent witnesses and the power to refuse a command. Independent measurements require blinded double-reviewed proposal registry with rejected actions and disagreement adjudication against human-designed or rule-based experimental planning with identical approved options and review time. Neither automation throughput nor a clean dashboard proves living biological function. The complete failed-attempt record remains part of the evidence. Consider objective-definition contract: an optimizer may pursue a surrogate rather than the intended scientific endpoint. An independent trial should pre-register explicit multiobjective target and forbidden moves. THE CROSS-FLAGSHIP VERIFICATION CONTRACT F151 may pass traceable batch identity, robot operation timing and status of independent qualification to F152, but it may not pass a presumed biological quality claim. F152 may share physical sensor status and external fault labels with F153, but a low alarm count is not permission to run the next experiment. F153 may propose new tests while an authorized human panel retains control of approval and veto. F154 receives only commands within its pre-authorized local hardware envelope; independent emergency-stop circuits cannot be overridden by an AI policy. F155 receives the typed protocol, calibration provenance and failed execution records, and tests whether another vendor device produces equivalent physical actions without privileged tuning. Every inter-flagship signal carries its unit, confidence bounds, timestamp, data lineage, authority and invalidity conditions. The thirty candidate mathematical relations in the PDF include accounting identities, sensor-performance ratios, timing budgets, review queue measures, dimensionless transfer loss and uncertainty-sensitive reproducibility scores. Each states its assumptions and dimensions. The forty-two three-dimensional models are explicitly synthetic and independently recalculable from raw numerical formulas and stored CSV triples. They are visualization and software-reconstruction exercises, not material validation. The eighty-two research chapters repeat a six-phase logic with different physical questions: physical identity and authorization, fair competing explanation, recomputed three-dimensional sensitivity, blinded independent measurement, benign counterfactual fault challenge, external transfer and permission to refuse. Their three literary and scientific voices are mechanism, measurement and refutation. A reader should find genuine scientific disagreement and a feasible negative answer, not merely an impressive number of pages. The two hundred Research Gates are planned future investigations with a distinct origin, an extreme counterworld and an independent research plan. They do not promise that robotic laboratories will be more accurate, biological samples more mature or quantum and AI computations magically faster than physical constraints permit. The thirty-three Phoenix prototypes are nonclinical and predominantly inert apparatus concepts: batch-accounting ledgers, blind sensor fault chambers, human veto interfaces, safe-state clocks and cross-device reference artifacts. Their purpose is to be built, modified, contradicted or retired by future engineers. An honest boundary is a durable scientific inheritance.
